The end of the object is the float at 0x102A24, so size = 0x102A28 = 1059368.
members: G_MainMP_AllocateGameMemory@0x14121C630 stores the vtable at +0 of the new object; BGVehicles is 8 bytes in IDA and nothing in Replay touches it otherwise (unchanged)

GVehicles::PhysicsInit@0x140E9EC20: `add rcx, 8` then `call GPhysicsVehicleManager__Init` (manager = this+8); GVehicles::PhysicsOnWorldAction@0x140E9EF50 and PhysicsAfterWorldStep@0x140E9D460 loop over 128 elements from this+8 with stride 3312. Size is at most 1044480 (the next subobject is at 0xFF008); not proven exact

G_MainMP_AllocateGameMemory: `BGVehicles_ctor(obj+1044488)` then vtable G_MainSubsystemBVftable_2464618 stored at obj+1044488; G_MainSP_AllocateGameMemory: `lea rcx, [rdi+0FF008h]` and the same vtable store. Room is 520 bytes (up to the suspend manager at 0xFF210). UNCONFIRMED: slot 2 is G_Vehicle_AddDirectionalImpactEvent, which suggests the event system, but the game-test event system is 528 bytes and does not fit in 520

G_MainMP_AllocateGameMemory: GVehicleSuspendManager_Init(obj+1045008) (0xFF210); G_MainSP_AllocateGameMemory: `lea rcx, [rdi+0FF210h]`. GVehicleSuspendManager_Init@0x140EA0410 writes 256 records of 32 bytes from +28, 2048 WORD index at +0x2000 and a count dword at +0x3000; SuspendVehicle@0x140EA07F0 uses `this+12288` as the next index. So size is 12292 to 12296 (next subobject at 0x102218), not 27652

G_MainMP_AllocateGameMemory: `*(QWORD*)(obj+1057304) = G_MainSubsystemAVftable_2464608`; G_MainSP_AllocateGameMemory: `mov [rdi+102218h], rax`. Nothing else is written there, so 8 bytes (vtable only). Vtable slots G_Physics_ResolvePairEntityLink and G_Vehicle_ProcessContactPair suggest collision (UNCONFIRMED name)

GVehicles::PhysicsAfterWorldStep@0x140E9D460: `lea rbx, [r14+102220h]` is the list base (8-byte entries, `p += 8` per entry, loop count from `mov eax, [r14+102A20h]`), and the count is reset by `mov [r14+102A20h], ebp`; SP allocator `mov [rdi+102A20h], r14d`. 256 entries x 8 + count 4 = 2052 bytes = VehicleScriptableDmg (m_scriptablesToDamage at +0, m_cursor at +2048)

GVehicles::PhysicsOnWorldAction@0x140E9EF50 end: `*(float*)(this+1059364) = deltaTime`; GVehicles::PhysicsInit@0x140E9EC20: `mov dword ptr [rbx+102A24h], 0`; GVehicles::PhysicsAfterWorldStep@0x140E9D460: `movss xmm1, [r14+102A24h]`

structs.notes: Size proven by allocation (1059368). The A129 packet is wrong in two places: the raw offsets are 0xFF210 = 1045008 (not 1044496), 0x102218 = 1057304 (not 1058840), 0x102220 = 1057312 and 0x102A20 = 1059360 (the first pass said the list is at 1058848 and that the 1057312 accesses were IDA-typed; the disassembly `lea rbx, [r14+102220h]` shows they are raw). PhysicsInit's typed write `m_suspendManager.m_infos[22]...partName = 0` is really a dword write at raw 0x102A24 (the float). The name GVehicles::~GVehicles at 0x140E9EF30 is wrong (see renames). Replay has no deleting destructor for GVehicles; the size comes from the allocators.

structs.name: GVehiclesSP
structs.size_evidence: method 1: G_MainSP_AllocateGameMemory@0x14182B080 allocates the SP object with `mov edx, 102A28h` (1059368) at 0x14182B3BF, the inlined GVehicles::AllocateMemory<GVehiclesSP> (the game-test source gives the same template, which allocates sizeof(GVehiclesSP) and memsets from m_vehiclePhysicsManager; game-test GetMemorySize<GVehiclesSP> returns the same size as GVehicles, 1087032 there, so the SP class adds no bytes in game-test either).
members: G_MainSP_AllocateGameMemory@0x14182B080 uses the GVehicles layout at offset 0 (manager at +8, suspend manager at 0xFF210, PhysicsInit with rdi = this at 0x14182B43D); the object is 1059368 bytes, so the derived class takes the base size
changed_members: IDA has one _pad0 of 1087032 bytes; should be GVehicles baseclass_0 (1059368). Changing it resizes the struct: coordinator action
unconfirmed: no SP-only member found: GVehiclesSP::FinishVehicleDamage@0x14185F150 only calls G_Vehicle_FinishDamage; GVehiclesSP::UpdateSpaceshipAnimscriptedMove@0x141860A00 touches only the Vehicle argument and entity; GVehiclesSP_SetDamageFinishedState@0x14185F1F0 writes the Vehicle argument at +1048, not this
structs.notes: Derived class with no own member read in Replay; size follows the SP allocation. The single-base layout is the proposal.

renames: not a destructor: its body is GVehicles_PhysicsLoadAllFromMemFile(this+8, ctx) plus BG_BSpline_Data_LoadFromMemFile(ctx); the game-test GVehicles::PhysicsLoad calls BgVehiclePhysicsManager::LoadAllFromSaveGame(&this->m_vehiclePhysicsManager, ...), the same manager at this+8.
